+# Adversarial review — issue 1156 / EQC-5
+
+## High
+
+- None found in Pass 1.
+
+## Medium
+
+- None found in Pass 1.
+
+### [Pass 3a] Deleting the `data-acq-skill-spec` handler exceeds AC #4's literal cleanup allowance
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `specs/stories/feature.1156.eqc5-remove-skill-acquisition.story.md:143` (contract); `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:2505` (the current location immediately after the deleted branch)
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Audit the implemented handler deletions against AC #4 literally. The AC explicitly enumerates `[data-skill-acq-spec]` and `[data-acq-skill]` for deletion, then says the shared “Add/Remove/dot/unknown/spec-chip handlers” are left in place and grants adjacent-cleanup discretion only to the Add/Remove `rowKey === 'skill'` ternaries. The change additionally deletes the distinct `[data-acq-skill-spec]`/`acqSkillSpec` handler; the Tasks section acknowledges that it was not enumerated in the original AC.
+- **Observable consequence:** There is no current player-facing failure because `_renderSkillRow`, the only emitter, is also deleted. However, the completed implementation does not satisfy the acceptance contract as written, so the story cannot truthfully be accepted without either narrowing/amending AC #4 or restoring dead code that the intended removal clearly no longer needs.
+- **Confidence:** High on the literal contradiction and on the handler being dead; the appropriate resolution is a spec correction rather than a runtime code rollback.
+
+## Low
+
+### [Pass 1] Add/Remove handler test does not prove the handlers are hardcoded to Resources
+
+- **Severity:** Low
+- **File:line:** `server/tests/issue-1156-eqc5-remove-skill-acquisition.test.js:131`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** A future or accidental edit deletes either delegated Add/Remove branch, changes it to read or write the wrong key, or otherwise breaks the handler while continuing not to contain the exact text `rowKey === 'skill'`.
+- **Observable consequence:** The test titled “Add/Remove row handlers hardcode acq_resource_rows” still passes even though it never asserts that either handler exists or that both read and write `acq_resource_rows`; a Resources acquisition regression can therefore pass this advertised guard.
+- **Confidence:** High. The sole assertion at line 134 is a whole-file negative match for the removed ternary text.
+
+### [Pass 1] Skill-markup removal test misses the removed `data-acq-skill-spec` attribute family
+
+- **Severity:** Low
+- **File:line:** `server/tests/issue-1156-eqc5-remove-skill-acquisition.test.js:90`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** `data-acq-skill-spec` or `data-acq-skill-spec-hidden` markup/handlers survive or are accidentally reintroduced without a direct `data-acq-skill="..."` attribute or the older, differently ordered `data-skill-acq-spec` spelling.
+- **Observable consequence:** The “no data-acq-skill … markup/handlers remain” test stays green because `/data-acq-skill[="[]/` deliberately cannot consume the hyphen after `data-acq-skill`, while the second assertion checks `data-skill-acq-spec`, not `data-acq-skill-spec`.
+- **Confidence:** High. Both missed spellings are visible in the deleted diff, and neither is matched by the two assertions.
+
+### [Pass 1] Legacy-annotation test checks for only one annotation, not every field named by its title
+
+- **Severity:** Low
+- **File:line:** `server/tests/issue-1156-eqc5-remove-skill-acquisition.test.js:179`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Any individual `skill_acq_*`, `skill_acquisitions`, or `acq_skill_rows` declaration loses its `[legacy]` annotation while at least one other `[legacy]` token remains within the 1,400-character slice.
+- **Observable consequence:** The test titled “the skill_acq_* fields are annotated [legacy]” passes despite incomplete schema documentation. The current diff does annotate the declarations; this is a regression-test precision issue, not a current schema defect.
+- **Confidence:** High. The test performs a single `toMatch(/\[legacy\]/)` against the entire slice.
+
+### [Pass 2] The acquisition gate definition still advertises the removed Skills channel
+
+- **Severity:** Low
+- **File:line:** `public/js/tabs/downtime-data.js:441`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Any consumer renders the exported `DOWNTIME_GATES` definition (or the dormant manual-gate UI is restored) after this change.
+- **Observable consequence:** The prompt still asks, “Do you want to use Resources or Skills to attempt to acquire anything?” even though the Skills acquisition channel and all of its write-side controls are gone. In the current form this label is dormant: `downtime-form.js` imports the array only to restore and collect gate values and contains no loop that renders `gate.label`, so there is no present player-facing break. It is nevertheless a contradictory source-of-truth value left by the removal and is not covered by the new tests.

import { MongoClient } from 'mongodb';
import { config } from './config.js';

let client;
let db;

// Pure decision logic for the test-DB safety guard — extracted so it can be
// unit-tested without a real MongoDB connection.
//
// Vitest sets process.env.VITEST truthy in every worker. If we're running
// under vitest, the resolved DB name MUST end with `_test` — otherwise a
// regression in setup-env.js ordering (or an env override) would silently
// point a test run at production.
export function assertTestDbSafety(dbName, isVitest) {
  if (isVitest && !dbName.endsWith('_test')) {
    throw new Error(
      `Refusing to connect: test context (VITEST) targeting non-test database '${dbName}'. ` +
        `Tests must use a *_test database — check tests/helpers/setup-env.js ordering.`
    );
  }
}

export async function connectDb() {
  if (db) return; // Already connected — idempotent for test suites sharing a process
  const dbName = process.env.MONGODB_DB || 'tm_suite';
  assertTestDbSafety(dbName, !!process.env.VITEST);
  // Strip legacy ssl= param — not accepted by MongoDB driver v7
  const uri = config.MONGODB_URI.replace(/[&?]ssl=[^&]*/g, '');
  client = new MongoClient(uri, {
    serverSelectionTimeoutMS: 5000,
    tls: true,
  });
  await client.connect();
  db = client.db(dbName);
  console.log('MongoDB connected successfully');
}

export function getDb() {
  if (!db) throw new Error('Database not connected — call connectDb() first');
  return db;
}

export function getCollection(name) {
  return getDb().collection(name);
}

// issue-1143: needed to start a session for multi-document transactions
// (office-actions.js's atomic budget-claim + dedupe + write).
export function getClient() {
  if (!client) throw new Error('MongoDB client not connected — call connectDb() first');
  return client;
}

// Returns true if the DB connection is alive
export function isConnected() {
  try {
    return !!db;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

export async function closeDb() {
  if (client) {
    await client.close();
    client = null;
    db = null;
    console.log('MongoDB connection closed');
  }
}

  48:   if (!sub) return next(); // existing handler returns 404
  49:   if (!sub.cycle_id) return next();
  50:   const cycleOid = sub.cycle_id instanceof ObjectId
  51:     ? sub.cycle_id
  52:     : parseId(String(sub.cycle_id));
  53:   if (!cycleOid) return next();
  54:   const cycle = await getCollection('downtime_cycles').findOne(
  55:     { _id: cycleOid },
  56:     { projection: { status: 1, phase: 1, out_of_window_player_ids: 1 } }
  57:   );
  58:   // CM-1 (#1028): phase-aware verdict, extracted pure so the matrix is
  59:   // unit-testable. Cycles carrying a known `phase` use the new lane (feeding
  60:   // fields writable in prep and game, general edits in downtime, ST always);
  61:   // cycles without one get the legacy status==='closed' gate byte-identical,
  62:   // including the out-of-window exception (issue #295).
  63:   const charIdStr = String(sub.character_id || '');
  64:   const oowIds = (cycle?.out_of_window_player_ids || []).map(String);
  65:   const verdict = openCycleVerdict({
  66:     cycle,
  67:     role: req.user?.role,
  68:     bodyKeys: Object.keys(req.body || {}),
  69:     oowMatch: !!charIdStr && oowIds.includes(charIdStr),
  70:   });
  71:   if (verdict === 'locked') {
  72:     return res.status(423).json({
  73:       error: 'CYCLE_CLOSED',
  74:       message: 'Cycle is closed; submissions are locked',
  75:     });

  51: /** Old bucket → new bucket. The one-to-one mapping this whole script exists to apply. */
  52: export const BUCKET_MAP = Object.freeze({
  53:   weapon: 'combat_gear',
  54:   armour: 'combat_gear',
  55:   equipment: 'skill_gear',
  56:   asset: 'container',
  57: });
  58: 
  59: const NEW_BUCKETS = new Set(['combat_gear', 'skill_gear', 'tool_utility', 'narrative', 'container']);
  60: 
  61: /**
  62:  * Compute the migration plan for a single catalogue document. Pure — no DB
  63:  * access, no module-level state.
  64:  *
  65:  * @param {object} doc - an equipment_catalogue document
  66:  * @returns {{ touched: boolean, fromBucket: string|undefined, toBucket: string|undefined, reason: string|null }}
  67:  */
  68: export function planBucketMigration(doc) {
  69:   if (!doc || typeof doc !== 'object') {
  70:     return { touched: false, fromBucket: undefined, toBucket: undefined, reason: 'malformed document' };
  71:   }
  72:   const from = doc.bucket;
  73:   // EQC-1 review patch (#1152, Codex external review Low finding): a
  74:   // non-string `bucket` (e.g. `['weapon']`) would otherwise reach
  75:   // `BUCKET_MAP[from]` and JS's implicit property-key coercion would stringify
  76:   // it to `'weapon'`, silently normalising a malformed document instead of
  77:   // flagging it for human review per this function's own "flag rather than
  78:   // guess" policy. Reject any non-string bucket explicitly, before either
  79:   // lookup.
  80:   if (typeof from !== 'string') {
  81:     return { touched: false, fromBucket: from, toBucket: undefined, reason: `bucket is not a string (got ${Array.isArray(from) ? 'array' : typeof from})` };
  82:   }
  83:   if (NEW_BUCKETS.has(from)) {
  84:     return { touched: false, fromBucket: from, toBucket: from, reason: null };
  85:   }
  86:   const to = BUCKET_MAP[from];
  87:   if (!to) {
  88:     // Neither a known old value nor a known new one — flag rather than guess.
  89:     return { touched: false, fromBucket: from, toBucket: undefined, reason: `unrecognised bucket value "${from}"` };
  90:   }
  91:   return { touched: true, fromBucket: from, toBucket: to, reason: null };
  92: }
  93: 
  94: /**
  95:  * Drive the migration against MongoDB. Returns the aggregate summary.
  96:  *
  97:  * @param {object} [opts]
  98:  * @param {boolean} [opts.dryRun]
  99:  * @param {boolean} [opts.log]
 100:  */
 101: export async function migrate(opts = {}) {
 102:   const { dryRun = true, log = true } = opts;
 103:   const col = getCollection('equipment_catalogue');
 104:   const docs = await col.find({}).toArray();
 105: 
 106:   const totals = {
 107:     scanned: docs.length,
 108:     touched: 0,
 109:     written: 0,
 110:     perMapping: Object.create(null),
 111:     unrecognised: [],
 112:     failedAt: null,
 113:   };
 114: 
 115:   // EQC-1 review patch (#1152, Codex external review Medium finding): the
 116:   // original version incremented `totals.touched` and logged the summary
 117:   // ONLY after the full loop completed, so a mid-loop `updateOne` failure
 118:   // (e.g. a transient Mongo disconnect) threw before an operator saw ANY
 119:   // record of what had already been written. `written` now tracks
 120:   // confirmed-successful writes separately from `touched` (planned writes),
 121:   // and the summary logs from inside a catch block too, so a partial-apply
 122:   // state is always visible even on failure.
 123:   try {
 124:     for (const doc of docs) {
 125:       const plan = planBucketMigration(doc);
 126:       if (plan.reason && !plan.touched) {
 127:         totals.unrecognised.push({ id: String(doc._id), name: doc.name || '(unnamed)', bucket: plan.fromBucket });
 128:         continue;
 129:       }
 130:       if (!plan.touched) continue;
 131: 
 132:       const key = `${plan.fromBucket} → ${plan.toBucket}`;
 133:       totals.perMapping[key] = (totals.perMapping[key] || 0) + 1;
 134:       totals.touched += 1;
 135: 
 136:       if (!dryRun) {
 137:         await col.updateOne({ _id: doc._id }, { $set: { bucket: plan.toBucket, updated_at: new Date().toISOString() } });
 138:         totals.written += 1;
 139:       }
 140:     }
 141:   } catch (err) {
 142:     totals.failedAt = { scannedSoFar: totals.touched, writtenSoFar: totals.written, error: String(err && err.message || err) };
 143:     if (log) logSummary(totals, dryRun);
 144:     throw err;
 145:   }
 146: 
 147:   if (log) logSummary(totals, dryRun);
 148:   return totals;
 149: }
 150: 
 151: export function logSummary(totals, dryRun) {
 152:   const verb = dryRun ? '[DRY RUN] would touch' : 'touched';
 153:   console.log(`Scanned ${totals.scanned} catalogue item(s); ${verb} ${totals.touched}.`);
 154:   if (totals.failedAt) {
 155:     console.log(`\nFAILED mid-run: ${totals.failedAt.writtenSoFar} write(s) confirmed committed before the error; ` +
 156:       `${totals.failedAt.scannedSoFar - totals.failedAt.writtenSoFar} more were planned but not yet attempted or did not complete. ` +
 157:       `This script is idempotent — re-run it (dry-run first) to pick up where it left off, rather than assuming a full re-apply is needed.`);
 158:     console.log(`Error: ${totals.failedAt.error}`);
 159:   }
 160:   if (Object.keys(totals.perMapping).length) {
 161:     console.log('Per-mapping:');
 162:     for (const [k, n] of Object.entries(totals.perMapping)) console.log(`  ${k.padEnd(24)} ${n}`);
 163:   }
 164:   if (totals.unrecognised.length) {
 165:     console.log(`\nUNRECOGNISED bucket values (${totals.unrecognised.length}) — SKIPPED, need human review:`);
 166:     for (const u of totals.unrecognised) console.log(`  ${u.name} (${u.id}): bucket="${u.bucket}"`);
 167:   }
 168: }
 169: 
 170: export async function main(argv = process.argv) {
 171:   const dryRun = !argv.includes('--apply');
 172:   console.log(`Mode: ${dryRun ? 'DRY RUN (read only; pass --apply to write)' : 'APPLY (will write)'}`);
 173:   console.log(`Target DB: ${process.env.MONGODB_DB || 'tm_suite'}`);
 174:   console.log('');
 175: 
 176:   await connectDb();
 177:   try {
 178:     await migrate({ dryRun });
 179:   } finally {
 180:     await closeDb();

+### [Pass 3a] Deleting the `data-acq-skill-spec` handler exceeds AC #4's literal cleanup allowance
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `specs/stories/feature.1156.eqc5-remove-skill-acquisition.story.md:143` (contract); `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:2505` (the current location immediately after the deleted branch)
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Audit the implemented handler deletions against AC #4 literally. The AC explicitly enumerates `[data-skill-acq-spec]` and `[data-acq-skill]` for deletion, then says the shared “Add/Remove/dot/unknown/spec-chip handlers” are left in place and grants adjacent-cleanup discretion only to the Add/Remove `rowKey === 'skill'` ternaries. The change additionally deletes the distinct `[data-acq-skill-spec]`/`acqSkillSpec` handler; the Tasks section acknowledges that it was not enumerated in the original AC.
+- **Observable consequence:** There is no current player-facing failure because `_renderSkillRow`, the only emitter, is also deleted. However, the completed implementation does not satisfy the acceptance contract as written, so the story cannot truthfully be accepted without either narrowing/amending AC #4 or restoring dead code that the intended removal clearly no longer needs.
+- **Confidence:** High on the literal contradiction and on the handler being dead; the appropriate resolution is a spec correction rather than a runtime code rollback.
+

+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `specs/stories/feature.1156.eqc5-remove-skill-acquisition.story.md:143` (contract); `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:2505` (the current location immediately after the deleted branch)
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Audit the implemented handler deletions against AC #4 literally. The AC explicitly enumerates `[data-skill-acq-spec]` and `[data-acq-skill]` for deletion, then says the shared “Add/Remove/dot/unknown/spec-chip handlers” are left in place and grants adjacent-cleanup discretion only to the Add/Remove `rowKey === 'skill'` ternaries. The change additionally deletes the distinct `[data-acq-skill-spec]`/`acqSkillSpec` handler; the Tasks section acknowledges that it was not enumerated in the original AC.
+- **Observable consequence:** There is no current player-facing failure because `_renderSkillRow`, the only emitter, is also deleted. However, the completed implementation does not satisfy the acceptance contract as written, so the story cannot truthfully be accepted without either narrowing/amending AC #4 or restoring dead code that the intended removal clearly no longer needs.
+- **Confidence:** High on the literal contradiction and on the handler being dead; the appropriate resolution is a spec correction rather than a runtime code rollback.
+

+- **Triggering input or sequence:** A future or accidental edit deletes either delegated Add/Remove branch, changes it to read or write the wrong key, or otherwise breaks the handler while continuing not to contain the exact text `rowKey === 'skill'`.

+- **Observable consequence:** The test titled “the skill_acq_* fields are annotated [legacy]” passes despite incomplete schema documentation. The current diff does annotate the declarations; this is a regression-test precision issue, not a current schema defect.
+- **Confidence:** High. The test performs a single `toMatch(/\[legacy\]/)` against the entire slice.

+### [Pass 2] The acquisition gate definition still advertises the removed Skills channel
+
+- **Severity:** Low
+- **File:line:** `public/js/tabs/downtime-data.js:441`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Any consumer renders the exported `DOWNTIME_GATES` definition (or the dormant manual-gate UI is restored) after this change.
+- **Observable consequence:** The prompt still asks, “Do you want to use Resources or Skills to attempt to acquire anything?” even though the Skills acquisition channel and all of its write-side controls are gone. In the current form this label is dormant: `downtime-form.js` imports the array only to restore and collect gate values and contains no loop that renders `gate.label`, so there is no present player-facing break. It is nevertheless a contradictory source-of-truth value left by the removal and is not covered by the new tests.
+- **Confidence:** High that the stale value exists and is not currently rendered; medium that it will affect a live consumer without a future rendering change.

+# Adversarial review — issue 1156 / EQC-5

+- None found.

+## Medium

+### [Pass 3a] Deleting the `data-acq-skill-spec` handler exceeds AC #4's literal cleanup allowance
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `specs/stories/feature.1156.eqc5-remove-skill-acquisition.story.md:143` (contract); `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:2505` (the current location immediately after the deleted branch)
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Audit the implemented handler deletions against AC #4 literally. The AC explicitly enumerates `[data-skill-acq-spec]` and `[data-acq-skill]` for deletion, then says the shared “Add/Remove/dot/unknown/spec-chip handlers” are left in place and grants adjacent-cleanup discretion only to the Add/Remove `rowKey === 'skill'` ternaries. The change additionally deletes the distinct `[data-acq-skill-spec]`/`acqSkillSpec` handler; the Tasks section acknowledges that it was not enumerated in the original AC.
+- **Observable consequence:** There is no current player-facing failure because `_renderSkillRow`, the only emitter, is also deleted. However, the completed implementation does not satisfy the acceptance contract as written, so the story cannot truthfully be accepted without either narrowing/amending AC #4 or restoring dead code that the intended removal clearly no longer needs.
+- **Confidence:** High on the literal contradiction and on the handler being dead; the appropriate resolution is a spec correction rather than a runtime code rollback.
+
+## Low
+
+### [Pass 1] Add/Remove handler test does not prove the handlers are hardcoded to Resources
+
+- **Severity:** Low
+- **File:line:** `server/tests/issue-1156-eqc5-remove-skill-acquisition.test.js:131`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** A future or accidental edit deletes either delegated Add/Remove branch, changes it to read or write the wrong key, or otherwise breaks the handler while continuing not to contain the exact text `rowKey === 'skill'`.
+- **Observable consequence:** The test titled “Add/Remove row handlers hardcode acq_resource_rows” still passes even though it never asserts that either handler exists or that both read and write `acq_resource_rows`; a Resources acquisition regression can therefore pass this advertised guard.
+- **Confidence:** High. The sole assertion at line 134 is a whole-file negative match for the removed ternary text.
+
+### [Pass 1] Skill-markup removal test misses the removed `data-acq-skill-spec` attribute family
+
+- **Severity:** Low
+- **File:line:** `server/tests/issue-1156-eqc5-remove-skill-acquisition.test.js:90`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** `data-acq-skill-spec` or `data-acq-skill-spec-hidden` markup/handlers survive or are accidentally reintroduced without a direct `data-acq-skill="..."` attribute or the older, differently ordered `data-skill-acq-spec` spelling.
+- **Observable consequence:** The “no data-acq-skill … markup/handlers remain” test stays green because `/data-acq-skill[="[]/` deliberately cannot consume the hyphen after `data-acq-skill`, while the second assertion checks `data-skill-acq-spec`, not `data-acq-skill-spec`.
+- **Confidence:** High. Both missed spellings are visible in the deleted diff, and neither is matched by the two assertions.
+
+### [Pass 1] Legacy-annotation test checks for only one annotation, not every field named by its title
+
+- **Severity:** Low
+- **File:line:** `server/tests/issue-1156-eqc5-remove-skill-acquisition.test.js:179`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Any individual `skill_acq_*`, `skill_acquisitions`, or `acq_skill_rows` declaration loses its `[legacy]` annotation while at least one other `[legacy]` token remains within the 1,400-character slice.
+- **Observable consequence:** The test titled “the skill_acq_* fields are annotated [legacy]” passes despite incomplete schema documentation. The current diff does annotate the declarations; this is a regression-test precision issue, not a current schema defect.
+- **Confidence:** High. The test performs a single `toMatch(/\[legacy\]/)` against the entire slice.
+
+### [Pass 2] The acquisition gate definition still advertises the removed Skills channel
+
+- **Severity:** Low
+- **File:line:** `public/js/tabs/downtime-data.js:441`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Any consumer renders the exported `DOWNTIME_GATES` definition (or the dormant manual-gate UI is restored) after this change.
+- **Observable consequence:** The prompt still asks, “Do you want to use Resources or Skills to attempt to acquire anything?” even though the Skills acquisition channel and all of its write-side controls are gone. In the current form this label is dormant: `downtime-form.js` imports the array only to restore and collect gate values and contains no loop that renders `gate.label`, so there is no present player-facing break. It is nevertheless a contradictory source-of-truth value left by the removal and is not covered by the new tests.
+- **Confidence:** High that the stale value exists and is not currently rendered; medium that it will affect a live consumer without a future rendering change.

The existing Vitest failures and stale-fixture Playwright failures are not caused by EQC-5.
